item.title: Red Sox's Triston Casas Hits Home Run In First At-Bat In 574 Days
item.description: Boston Red Sox first baseman Triston Casas The Major League Baseball Season may be over, but baseball is still happening around the world. The Dominican Winter League is one of the premier winter leagues, and this year, Triston Casas is playing for the Tigres Del Licey. On Friday night, he played in his first game of the season and hit a grand slam in the bottom of the first inning. TRISTON CASAS GRAND SLAM IN HIS FIRST LIDOM PA SINCE OCT 2022 pic.twitter.com/tNNrDspcHB — Sarah Langs (@SlangsOnSports) November 28, 2026 It was Casas' first at-bat in any league since May 2, 2025, 574 days ago. This is Casas' second time suiting up for the Tigres Del Licey. The first stint he had in the Dominican Winter League came in 2022. His grand slam was his lone hit of the game, but it is a potential sign of what's to come when he's back in the big leagues. Casas was great in the only big league season in which he played over 130 games. In 2023, he slashed .263/.367/.490 with 24 home runs. However, he has battled injuries ever since. In 2024, he missed 99 games with torn cartilage in his rib cage, but still hit 13 home runs with a .800 OPS in 63 games. In 2025, he got off to a slow start and then ruptured his left patellar tendon. He missed the rest of the year, suffered setbacks this year, and missed all of the 2026 season. This year, he dealt with an abdominal strain and underwent wrist surgery. Things are different now for the Red Sox than they were the last time Casas played. They have a new starting first baseman, and with Jake Bauers also on the team, Casas may not even be the backup. At-bats will be hard to come by for him, and he could be traded. item.title: Kentucky basketball’s illegal in-bounds play has fans creating Mark Pope replacement lists
item.description: (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mark Pope entered the year with Kentucky men’s basketball desperately needing a signature season and a deep NCAA tournament run to save his job and regain the momentum of the program. Instead, Pope’s Wildcats are already in danger of missing March Madness less than a month into the 2026-27 campaign after suffering their third embarrassing loss so far on Friday night. Wichita State beat Kentucky, 73-71 in overtime, on a loss that can be blamed directly on coaching. Kentucky already got destroyed by Kansas in the Champions Classic, then lost handily to a good-not-great Indiana team. This Wichita State loss feels like the new low point of the Pope era, not because the Shockers are bad — they’re now ranked nine spots ahead of Kentucky on KenPom — but because of how the Wildcats lost. Pope was booed off the floor at home as he walked off the court after the loss to Wichita State. He deserved it for how poorly he managed the end of the game. Kentucky should have had one last chance to tie or win the game down two with 5.4 seconds remaining in overtime. Pope went into the huddle and drew up a play that directly resulted in a turnover. The Wildcats tried to get tricky inbounding the ball under their own basket, but Pope’s play was illegal for passing the ball across the baseline. This is as humiliating as it gets for a coach already under fire. Kentucky inbound turnover pic.twitter.com/ryIWoB4QPo — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Pope took full accountability for the play after the game. “That’s 100% on me, guys. That is 100% me. Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. And it’s really costly. It’s a tough one to carry as a coach, for sure. Kentucky’s final play wasn’t their only miscue. Down two with 35 seconds left, Pope drew up a play for his $6 million man Milan Momcilovic , who promptly stepped out of bounds. Watch the play here: Milan Momcilovic steps out of bounds wow pic.twitter.com/SjqzMju5dN — wok (@wokdior) November 28, 2026 Kentucky actually did get one more chance to win the game after the illegal play on the baseline. Wichita State turned the ball over on the next possession, and Momcilovic got a decent look at a game-winning three, but missed. What this comes down to is poor execution by Kentucky, and it has Big Blue Nation ready to move on. item.title: Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the second practice of the Formula 1 2026 Qatar Grand Prix, at Lusail International Circuit. (is associated with: «Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in final practice for F1 Qatar GP») Alessio Morgese/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa World champion Kimi Antonelli led a third Mercedes one-two ahead of team-mate George Russell in the final practice for the Formula One Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday. The top two was a repetition of the previous two practice sessions on Friday. The Italian clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 22.400 seconds, beating Russell by 0.249 seconds. Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third ahead of team-mate Isack Hadjar. Charles Leclerc of Ferrari was fifth, with the McLaren duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri right behind in sixth and seventh respectively. Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton was ninth in the other Ferrari. The race in Qatar is taking place despite continuing security concerns due to conflicts in the Middle East. Several broadcasters and other personnel decided against attending the penultimate race of the season. Williams driver Carlos Sainz, who was 18th in practice, revealed on Thursday that drivers were briefed on emergency evacuation procedures and was surprised to discover journalists knew nothing about it. "I was told there was such a plan, and I expected the press would be included, too," he said. Qualifying for Sunday's showdown is later on Saturday. There's nothing more at stake at this point of the year, as Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' title and Mercedes have claimed the constructors' championship.

item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson #14 and referees attempt to keep Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf #4 from lunging at Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean #33 during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburg Steelers on November 22nd, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers rallied the troops and dominated the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos on Black Friday in Acrisure Stadium, 27-5. However, less than 24 hours after the win, the Steelers’ top receiver is back in the headlines after being fined by the NFL for his actions during the team’s Week 11 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported on Saturday that the league has fined Metcalf a total of $26,867 for several infractions that occurred during the Steelers’ Week 11 game. The receiver was ejected from the Steelers game against the Eagles after receiving his second personal foul of the game for an altercation with Philadelphia defensive back Cooper DeJean. It looked as though Metcalf was trying to poke the eyes of the defensive back, but the receiver has denied those allegations. Although Metcalf has not been clear about what exactly transpired on the field, it landed him in the headlines for all the wrong reasons. The game marked the third ejection in the career of Metcalf, his first since 2023 and his first as a Steeler. Some expected Metcalf to receive a suspension from the league office for the repeat offense, but the league said he would not be suspended and could still face fines. item.description: Nations Championship Wales (26) 40 Tries: Adams 2, Murray, Morgan-Williams, Morgan 2 Cons: Costelow 5 Japan (0) 10 Tries: Komura, Vailea Wales finished their Nations Championship campaign with another victory against Japan in a six-try display at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. Wing Josh Adams and replacement flanker Jac Morgan claimed two tries apiece, with full-back Blair Murray and scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams also dotting down, while player of the match Sam Costelow kicked 10 points. This set up the most comprehensive margin of victory of the Steve Tandy coaching era in a match that was affected by the miserable conditions. Despite the scoreline, Wales again spent large periods of the game defending against a weakened Japan side who managed two late tries through replacements Shinya Komura and Halatoa Vailea. Returning flanker James Botham made 38 tackles as he equalled Dafydd Jenkins' world record effort in the 35-28 win against New Zealand, a mark they now both share with Thierry Dusautoir of France. It was a curious contest, low on quality, played in front of a half-empty Twickenham as part of a double-header before England faced New Zealand. The victory means Wales secured ninth in the inaugural Nations Championship and finished the year ninth in World Rugby's rankings. It was a second win in the space of three weeks against Japan, and a third victory in a November campaign that will forever be remembered for Wales beating New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. Wales struggle to create early energy Wales had unconvincingly defeated Japan 28-21 in the opening game of the November series, following up that with the famous win against the All Blacks before a narrow loss to Australia. Both Wales and Japan had finished fifth in their respective hemisphere sections to set up a fifth contest between Wales and Japan inside 17 months. Eddie Jones' side had suffered heavy 60-point defeats to England and Scotland and were down to the bare bones with flanker Tiennan Costley named on the wing. Wales initially made five changes with Morgan-Williams making his first Test start and prop Rhys Carre, hooker Ryan Elias, lock Adam Beard and Botham also included. With hooker Dewi Lake and Morgan dropping to the bench, lock Dafydd Jenkins captained the side for the first time in more than two years. There was another late alteration when wing Louis Rees-Zammit was ruled out because of illness, with Scarlets back Ellis Mee promoted from the bench for his first action of this November campaign. item.title: Bucks add games against Jazz and Raptors to schedule
item.description: Following the conclusion of preliminary NBA Cup play late on Nov. 27, the league added two regular-season games to the December schedule for teams that did not advance to the knockout rounds of the in-season tournament. The Milwaukee Bucks were one of those teams, and they had games against the Utah Jazz and Toronto Raptors added to their schedule. Milwaukee will head to Utah on Dec. 6 for a 4 p.m. CT game and host the Raptors on Dec. 10 at 7 p.m. CT. The Jazz game is an interesting addition, as the Bucks already had a trip to Salt Lake City on their schedule Jan. 26 as part of a West Coast trip. The game against the Raptors also will be the team's fourth meeting of the season and second at Fiserv Forum. The teams already have played twice, including the Bucks' second win of the season on Nov. 23. item.title: Skip Bayless says Cowboys would’ve won vs Eagles if they had made the Dak Prescott trade he told them to
item.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images Skip Bayless has continued to express his displeasure for Dak Prescott on the back of the Dallas Cowboys losing to the Philadelphia Eagles. The Cowboys are now 5-7 for the season after giving up 21 points against the Eagles, meaning there is a strong chance they will now go three years in a row without reaching the postseason. But rather than questioning Dallas’ defence, which is the worst in the league right now, Bayless has instead spoken of his desire to trade Dak Prescott for Jayden Daniels. Skip Bayless thinks Jayden Daniels would have helped the Dallas Cowboys beat the Philadelphia Eagles Bayless already commented on his desire to trade Prescott for Daniels prior to the November trade deadline. Speaking in late October, he said: “If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It’s done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I’ll take it. He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He’s been available this year; we’re 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels.” Now, on the latest episode of Gridiron, Bayless has once again been speaking about trading for Daniels and this time claimed that the quarterback ‘gets that game home’ [against the Eagles]. He said: “If there’s some way that Washington would trade me Jayden Daniels straight up for Dak Prescott, which they would laugh at, I would do it in a heartbeat because I’ve got 25 years old versus 33, and I’ve got the clutch gene versus no clutch gene. That’s just me.” His fellow host replied: “Yeah, and you still would have lost 38-39 yesterday,” seeing Skip respond by suggesting Daniels would have won them the game. He said: “No, I would not have. Jayden Daniels gets that game home. He’s going to just keep on keeping on in the fourth quarter. He’s going to throw two more touchdown passes in the fourth quarter.” While Skip seems keen to move on from Prescott, Daniels’ stats have not been that impressive this season. He has 1,788 passing yards (3,340 for Dak), 10 passing touchdowns versus 27 for the Cowboys star and has a completion rate of 64.9% compared to 65.8% for Prescott. Bayless also mentioned Daniels having a ‘clutch gene’, which may be the only area he actually has the better of the Dallas QB. Prescott is 2-5 in postseason games throughout his career, while the Washington Commanders star is 2-1. item.title: GB miss out on Davis Cup final as Alcaraz stars for Spain
item.description: Great Britain were unable to give Leon Smith the perfect send-off as Davis Cup captain as Carlos Alcaraz inspired Spain to a 2-0 victory in the semi-finals. Competing in their first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019, Britain fell short as Arthur Fery was unable to match the dazzling brilliance of Alcaraz, with the seven-time major winner surging to an emphatic 6-2 6-1 win. That was after rising star Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening singles match to put Spain in the driving seat in Bologna. The defeat brings the curtain down on Smith's near 17-year tenure as captain, during which he led Britain to Davis Cup success in 2015. Spain captain David Ferrer, who is also stepping down after this year's tournament, will have the chance to guide his nation to their first Davis Cup title since 2019 when they face Italy in Sunday's final. Three-time defending champions Italy beat Spain in last year's final , although they are without talisman and world number two Jannik Sinner because of a wrist injury that will keep him out of the Australian Open. "It is a second straight final, it is going to be my first Davis Cup final, I'll do whatever it takes to win," said Alcaraz. "It's something I have been chasing for a really long time, to be in a Davis Cup final." Alcaraz back to brilliant best against Fery as Norrie loses After Norrie's defeat by Jodar, Fery was faced with the mammoth task of beating world number three Alcaraz - a player he had never faced before. Alcaraz lifted his first ATP Finals title six days earlier, a triumph that completed his astonishing return to the sport following four months out with a wrist injury. And his return to top form was on full display as he dismantled Fery, ranked 32nd, in a dominant first set in which he dropped just two points behind his first serve. Alcaraz's movement and shot-making continued to dazzle the crowd in Italy and Fery could do little to stop the Spaniard's sprint to the finish line. Alcaraz started the season by becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam with his Australian Open triumph, and now has the chance to end the year with his first Davis Cup title, one of the few trophies he has yet to win. For Fery, who enjoyed his career-best season and a fairytale run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, it was another harsh reminder of the gulf in class between himself and the game's top players after he fell in straight sets to world number one Alexander Zverev in Thursday's quarter-final. item.title: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli completes practice clean sweep as Mercedes dominates
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli has handed Mercedes a clean sweep of Qatar GP practice sessions as the Silver Arrows head to qualifying with a huge advantage. Russell went quickest before halfway as teams embarked on soft-tyre runs with Mercedes continuing its ominous form on the high-downforce motorcycle circuit of Lusail, only for Antonelli to take another chunk out of that laptime in the second half. Unlike Friday's twice red-flagged FP2 session, third practice took place without incident, which was partly thanks to a tepid start with little to no action early on. At the start, Pierre Gasly circulated by himself, making up for lost ground after beaching his Alpine in the gravel midway through Friday's second practice. Gasly was eventually joined by team-mate Franco Colapinto and Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, while the others stayed in the garage for the first third of the session. That all changed suddenly before the 20-minute mark as the heavy hitters embarked on soft-tyre runs - a compound projected to be only useful for qualifying. The race is expected to be completed on medium and hard Pirelli tyres, which are facing their most demanding weekend on the Lusail loop. As qualifying simulations got underway, outgoing world champion Lando Norris headed to the Turn 14 escape road after catching a violent snap of oversteer. As was the case during both of Friday's practice endeavours, Mercedes immediately took charge with George Russell's 1m22.983s leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli. That was over half a second better than what McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen could muster, the latter driving a Red Bull RB22 which required rebalancing after a tougher free practice outing. While Russell then drifted wide in Turn 5, Antonelli's second mid-session run yielded a time almost identical to his team-mate's, just 0.017s off. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes With 15 minutes to go, Verstappen briefly claimed top before Antonelli immediately retaliated and restored Mercedes' comfortable half-second cushion with a 1m22.400s effort. Russell had no answer for that flash of pace, conceding 0.249s. Verstappen remained third, a sobering 0.501s in arrears as the first non-Mercedes car, followed by team-mate Isack Hadjar. After a Friday which Charles Leclerc described as "very difficult", there was little progress for Ferrari as Leclerc took fifth, eight tenths behind Antonelli. McLaren also struggled more than was expected with sixth for Norris and seventh for Piastri. Lewis Hamilton fared worse after being held up by traffic on his final hotlap, splitting Racing Bull's midfield leaders Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in ninth. item.description: Arizona Diamondbacks infielder Demetrio Crisantes (5) tracks a pop-up against the Seattle Mariners at Salt River Fields on March 9, 2026. The Arizona Diamondbacks made two notable additions on Friday, agreeing to a one-year, $3 million deal with Japanese right-hander Kona Takahashi and acquiring catcher Henry Davis from the Pittsburgh Pirates in exchange for utilityman Tim Tawa. Takahashi, 29, spent nine seasons with the Seibu Lions of Nippon Professional Baseball. He posted a 2.54 ERA over 138.1 innings in 2026 and brings a ground-ball-heavy approach after more than 1,300 career innings in Japan. As an international free agent with nine years of NPB service, he was not subject to a posting fee. The deal gives Arizona a low-cost rotation option as the club looks to manage payroll while addressing starting pitching depth. Earlier Friday, the Diamondbacks completed a one-for-one trade that sent Tawa to Pittsburgh for Davis, the former No. 1 overall pick in the 2021 draft. Davis has yet to establish himself as a regular in the majors but provides additional catching depth behind the current group. item.title: Ole Miss finishes season with fourth straight Egg Bowl win
item.description: OXFORD, MISSISSIPPI - NOVEMBER 27: Trinidad Chambliss #6 of the Mississippi Rebels celebrates after the game after defeating the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on November 27, 2026 in Oxford, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ole Miss overcame a slow offensive start, and once everything clicked, it caused a blowout in the Egg Bowl for a fourth straight win over Mississippi State, 41-17. The Rebels (8-4, 5-4 SEC) could not string together things offensively in the first half scoring only two field goals and trying a desperation 60-yard field goal at the end of the second quarter. Going into the locker room down 10-6, the boo’s were very audible through Vaught-Hemingway, and either those signs of unhappiness from the fans or a fire and brimstone speech from coaches or both lit a collective fire under Ole Miss. In the second half, Ole Miss outscored MSU 35-7 to completely overwhelm the Bulldogs. One of the major turning points in the game was the Blake Purchase interception to give the Rebels an extra possession but also prime field position after the turnover. I still think he scored on the play, but it didn’t really matter when it came to the final score. Trinidad Chambliss had 249 total offensive yards and three touchdowns, and he dealt with drops from his receiving corps early on that stalled drives plus the absence of three running backs from the usual rotation. Give it up to Joshua Dye for stepping up in the season finale going 20 carries for 91 yards and two touchdowns in a workman-like effort. The Ole Miss defense showed its moxie as well with seven sacks and 13 tackles for loss in the game. Suntarine Perkins led the way with 1.5 sacks and three TFL with his potential comeback to Oxford hanging in the air. MSU owned time of possession with 33:22 of the clock and was clearly trying to keep the Ole Miss offense off the field by running the ball for 131 total yards. The Bulldogs couldn’t convert on third downs, however, and the Purchase interception was the rope slipping out of your hands in a tug of war. For a lot of players, Friday was the last time they’ll play in VHS including Chambliss. Many of them will get to say they never lost an Egg Bowl. While the Golden Egg has taken more of a backseat in terms of accomplishment for Ole Miss teams, it is still an important game for fans and for former players. Damn good job the last four years, cheers! Ole Miss will await its bowl game destination next weekend. Current projections have the Rebels in the Reliaquest Bowl in Tampa, Fla. most likely and facing a Big Ten opponent yet to be determined by this Saturday’s games.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
